facts.text: The model predicts 621.70 N for the original car and 621.57 N for the synthetically dented car: -0.122 N (-0.020%). This is predicted aerodynamic change, not a damage or safety score.

This is a prescribed synthetic hood dent. Its geometry passed screening and the original and dented surfaces were evaluated separately. It is an aerodynamic demonstration, not a simulation of a crash or an assessment of structural damage or roadworthiness.
The synthetic hood dent moved the surface inward by at most 11.302 mm. The viewer opens at true scale. The colored patch shows geometric displacement, not measured damage severity.
The protected part of the car, including the passenger cabin, stayed exactly in place.

Inspect the localized movement, pressure and predicted airflow differences. Home photo or scan inspection is not implemented. This demonstration cannot identify internal damage, estimate repair costs or decide whether a real car is safe to drive.
This run used a trained prediction model. It has not been checked by an independent physics-based flow simulation or a wind tunnel.

technicalFacts.text: The model was trained for aerodynamic prediction, not collision damage assessment. A dent is an unverified input shape. Neither a small drag change nor a passing geometry check establishes that a damaged vehicle is safe.
The local run took 152.7 seconds including preparation and checks. The original-car calculation took 60.9 seconds. Testing the changed car took 61.8 seconds.
Sensitivity highlights where the model thinks a small shape change could affect air resistance. It is a suggestion to test, not proof that a change will help.
